title: Unify prefetch, deferred-ack and saga protocol for consumer stability
creator: Rashmi Kapoor
description:
Problem: Multiple consumer instability incidents over the last quarter traced to interaction between aggressive prefetching, eager ack-on-receive semantics, and a lack of coordinated retry/saga mechanics across Redis and Kafka based workers. Symptoms: tenant-level contention, spikes of duplicate processing after transient infra failures, and long tail latency when KV cache misses cascade into synchronous downstream writes.

Goal: Replace the ad-hoc prefetch + immediate-ack behavior with a unified consumer protocol that: 1) uses cooperative prefetch with per-tenant soft limits, 2) switches to deferred-ack (ack after durable side-effects), and 3) introduces a lightweight saga coordinator for multi-step work across queues to guarantee exactly-once-like outcomes without global locking. The change should reduce duplicate runs, improve latency tailSLO, and make backpressure predictable.

Scope: Redis stream consumers (current majority of async jobs) and Kafka ingress adapters used by the large-batch pipelines. Includes: upgrade of redis client to v1.9 (for improved async pool), refactor of consumer loop to event-loop friendly yield points, new DeferredAck helper library, saga-coordinator interface (in-process with pluggable persistence), tenant-level inflight counters, and metrics/dashboards for visibility.

Non-goals: Full distributed transaction semantics, complete rework of the worker fleet autoscaler (separate ticket), changing message format or public APIs to callers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Consumer tests simulate transient failures and show duplicates reduced by >=90% compared to baseline. 2) End-to-end visible metrics: per-tenant inflight_count, deferred_ack_lag, and saga-retries present in dashboards. 3) No latency tail regressions >5% at p99 across staging load tests. 4) Gradual rollout plan executed (staging -> canary on non-critical tenants -> 50% -> full), with rollback hooks validated. 5) PRs merged with integration tests and a runbook for incident recovery.
comments: 2025-09-13 - Triage: identified as P1 due to customer-visible duplicate processing during two incidents in Sept. Assigned to Connor for spike+design.

2025-09-18 - Spike complete: tested redis client v1.9 against our connection churn patterns. Observed 20% fewer connection re-creates under synthetic high-churn. Spike notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Deferred+Ack+Spike

2025-09-22 - Design review: opted for cooperative prefetch (soft token bucket per tenant) rather than strict leasing to keep latency low. Trade-offs documented in design doc; chose in-process saga coordinator persisted in Redis to avoid new infra. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Prefetch+DeferredAck+Design

2025-09-25 - Implementation: landed DeferredAck helper and per-tenant inflight counters in feature branch. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/worker-runtime/pull/1284 (DeferredAck), https://github.com/redwood-inference/worker-runtime/pull/1291 (prefetch tokens), https://github.com/redwood-inference/worker-runtime/pull/1302 (saga coordinator).

2025-09-29 - Load test: ran staging load test with 10k qps for 1 hour. Observed deferred_ack_lag median 45ms, p99 420ms. Duplicate rate decreased ~87% for the tested failure injection case. Some tenants still saw spikes due to long-running downstream writes; plan to add bounded async write buffering for those tenants.

2025-10-01 - Code review notes: PM and Reliability requested stronger observability (tagging by customer_tier and route). Added tracing hooks to DeferredAck and saga coordinator. Security requested a short review of Redis persistence keys (done).

2025-10-03 - Canary started: enabling new protocol for internal-noncritical tenants (10% traffic). Monitoring dashboards: Datadog dashboard 'async.consumer.prefetch' and 'async.consumer.saga' live. Canary will run 72 hours before 50% rollout.
Follow-ups: create separate ticket to add autoscaler signals from saga backpressure metrics; warn teams about minor schema change to internal telemetry names.
